TO:  JOSEPH M. HOEFGEN, CITY MANAGER

FROM:  ALLAN RIGG, PLANNING DIRECTOR

SUBJECT:  RESOLUTION R11-07; AFFIRMING THE PLANNING COMMISSION
  APPROVAL OF NC-1400/GA-1479/M-791-10; NEIGHBORHOOD
  COMPATIBILITY, GRADING, AND MISCELLANEOUS APPLICATIONS
  FOR A NEW SINGLE FAMILY RESIDENCE LOCATED AT 700 VIA
  HORCADA. LOT 12, BLOCK 1426, TRACT 8523.

DATE:  MARCH 8, 2011

The Issue

Should the City Council adopt Resolution 11-07 affirming the Planning Commission approval of
NC-1400/GA-1479/M-791-10; Neighborhood Compatibility, Grading, and Miscellaneous
applications for a new single family residence located at 700 Via Horcada?

Background and Analysis

On January 25, 2011, the City Council conducted a public hearing to consider the appeal of the
Planning Commission’s approval of NC-1400/GA-1479/M-791-10; Neighborhood Compatibility,
Grading, and Miscellaneous applications for a new single family residence located at 700 Via
Horcada. After considering the facts and testimony, the City Council voted (4-0) to continue the
public hearing to the appellant’s site at 702 Via Horcada.

The site visit was held on February 15, 2011 and focused on Section D of Neighborhood
Compatibility Chapter 18.36.030 which states that “designs should consider to the extent reasonably
practicable neighbors’ existing views”. Following the site visit, the City Council immediately
reconvened at City Hall for a formal discussion.

After considering the facts and testimony, the City Council voted (5-0) to affirm the Planning
Commission approval of NC-1400/GA-1479/M-791-10; Neighborhood Compatibility, Grading, and
Miscellaneous applications for a new single family residence located at 700 Via Horcada, with the
following additional conditions:

  1. The roof ridge shall be reduced by 1.5 ft.
  2. The trees on the eastern property line shall be removed.
  3. Vegetation along the eastern property line shall not exceed the height of the approved
  roof ridge line.
CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
MARCH 8, 2011
  4
   4. The barbecue and trellis shall be constructed outside of the side yard setback.

Please note that the original condition for a standard urban stormwater mitigation plan still applies
and is noted in the attached resolution.

This resolution confirms that decision.

Alternatives Available to Council

The following alternatives are available to the City Council:

  1.  Adopt resolution R11-07; affirming the Planning Commission approval of NC-
  1400/GA-1479/M-791-10; Neighborhood Compatibility, Grading, and Miscellaneous
  applications for a new single family residence located at 700 Via Horcada, with
  additional conditions.
  2.  Decline to act.

Recommendation from Staff

It is recommended that the City Council adopt Resolution R11-07; a Resolution of the City Council
of the City of Palos Verdes Estates, California, affirming the Planning Commission approval of NC-
1400/GA-1479/M-791-10; Neighborhood Compatibility, Grading, and Miscellaneous applications
for a new single family residence located at 700 Via Horcada, with additional conditions.

FROM:  ALEXA D. DAVIS, ADMINISTRATIVE ANALYST

SUBJECT:  SPECIAL EVENT APPLICATION FOR THE AMERICAN DIABETES
  ASSOCIATION TO HOLD CYCLING EVENT, "TOUR DE CURE," SUNDAY,
  MAY 1, 2011

DATE:  MARCH 8, 2011

THE ISSUE

Shall the City Council approve a Special Event Application by the American Diabetes Association to
hold its “Tour de Cure” Cycling Event on Sunday, May 1, 2011 from 7:00 a.m. to 12:30 p.m.?

BACKGROUND AND ANALYSIS

The American Diabetes Association is requesting permission to hold a portion of their “Tour de Cure”
ride through Palos Verdes Estates. This event raises funds for the American Diabetes Association’s
diabetes research, education and advocacy programs. It has previously been held successfully in the
City four times with minimal disruption.

The "Tour de Cure" will begin and end in Long Beach. The Palos Verdes leg enters through Via
Campesina to Via Corta. The route continues south on Palos Verdes Drive West exiting right onto
Paseo del Mar beyond Bluff Cove and continuing south until exiting east on Paseo Lunado and south
onto Palos Verdes Drive West. Tour maps are attached for your review.

An estimated 400 riders are expected to enter and exit the city in a staggered manner over a four-hour
period. The Police Department requires that the cyclists obey all traffic laws. Safety and monitoring of
riders’ progress is also provided by the American Diabetes Association staff and volunteers. Based on
the success of prior events by this organization, the traffic impact should be minor.

The Special Event Application has been preliminarily approved by all departments. All fees have been
paid and the Certificate of Insurance and Indemnification Agreement have been received.

ALTERNATIVES AVAILABLE TO THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  Council may approve the Special Event Application for the American Diabetes Association’s
  "Tour de Cure" Cycling Event.
CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
MARCH 8, 2011
  6
 2.  Council may choose not to approve the Special Event Application.

3.  Council may impose additional conditions or restrictions on the sponsors of the event.

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the City Council approve the Special Event Application for the
American Diabetes Association “Tour de Cure” to be held on Sunday, May 1, 2011 from 7:00 a.m. –
12:30 p.m.

TO:  JOSEPH M. HOEFGEN, CITY MANAGER

FROM:  ALEXA D. DAVIS, ADMINISTRATIVE ANALYST

SUBJECT:  REVIEW OF CITY POLICY REGARDING POSTING OF PROMOTIONAL AND
  DIRECTIONAL SIGNS ON PUBLIC PROPERTY

DATE:  MARCH 8, 2011

ISSUE

Review of City Policy Regarding Posting Promotional and Directional Signs on Public Property in
Palos Verdes Estates.

BACKGROUND

Throughout the course of the year, the City of Palos Verdes Estates receives numerous requests
from organizations wishing to post promotional signs at the two pre-designated median strips
adjacent to (1) Malaga Cove Plaza at Via Corta and (2) across from the Lunada Bay Fountain area.
In any given year, the City receives an estimated 30 requests for the posting of signs, and over the
past three years, the number of signs actually posted has ranged from 18 to 21 each year with each
sign posted for a maximum of one week. In addition to the “once per year events”, the Malaga
Cove site has been used for the placement of a library book sale sign which is posted monthly for
two days at a time. A five-year history showing prior year postings of signs is provided as
Attachment A to this report.

There is a substantial history associated with the City of Palos Verdes Estates’ efforts to craft a
policy intended to preserve the unique ambience of the City by limiting the posting of signs on
public property. A policy regarding posting promotional and directional signs on public property
was first adopted in 1993 to supplement the Palos Verdes Estates Municipal Code Chapter 8.20.050
(see Attachment B). The 1993 policy only permitted signs to be posted for City sponsored and City
recreational club events, and those benefiting the Palos Verdes Peninsula Unified School District’s
(PVUSD) educational program and the Peninsula Public Library. A copy of the 1993 policy is
provided as Attachment C.

Thirteen years later, in July and October 2006, the City Council received reports and provided
direction resulting in a revised sign policy, which was formally approved by the Council on October
10, 2006. In addition to the posting of signs for City, PVUSD, and Palos Verdes Library District
events, the 2006 policy provided a way for events sponsored by non-profit entities (where all
CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
MARCH 8, 2011
  8
 members were residents and/or property owners of the City) to seek City-sponsorship through the
Special Event Application process in order to gain approval to post signs. Additionally, the 2006
policy reduced the time of posting from two weeks to one week and established a first-come, first-
served priority for posting of signs. Attachment D includes a copy of the 2006 policy and the
associated minutes from the Council discussion/adoption at that time. Additionally, Attachment E
shows a redline version of the 1993 policy versus the 2006 policy.

As previously referenced, there are, on average, approximately 19 signs approved for posting for
one week in a given year. Additionally, there are approximately 12 signs promoting the Friends of
the Library Book Sale posted 2 days each month. In 4+ years since the 2006 policy was put in
place, the number of sign requests have increased. Several recent requests have presented
challenges to determine whether the organization making the sign request falls within the purview
of the current sign policy. Over the past few months, the City received five such requests –
prompting the need to generate this staff report and to seek Council direction regarding the existing
sign policy.

ANALYSIS

Staff recently reviewed the sign policy with the City Attorney’s office and sought input on available
course of action for the City. The City Attorney’s office has raised concerns with the City
maintaining its existing policy as is and suggests that the City enact one of the following possible
options:

  1. Modify the policy to enact a time, place and manner regulation that would be
  Constitutionally permissible and place a responsible limit on the number of signs
  permitted. While the City can specify that commercial signs are prohibited in the right
  of way, the options are limited for how the City is able to regulate non-commercial
  signage. For example, the City may not limit the content (what is promoted) or speaker
  (organization). In doing so, the City may impose objective standards limiting size and
  height, the number of days an individual sign may be posted at a particular location, and
  limit the total number of signs permitted each year. These types of restrictions are
  known as time, place, and manner restrictions; or

  2. Discontinue the City Policy Regarding Posting Promotional and Directional Signs on
  Public Property. This option would completely ban the placement of signs within the
  public right-of-way for all organizations -- including City sponsored events.

One other factor that Council may wish to consider is whether the need really exists today (as
compared to prior years) for organizations to use public property to post promotional signs for
special events. Unlike just a few years ago, it is commonplace for organizations to publicize events
through e-mail announcements, web page advertising, and direct mailing to the target audience.
These direct marketing methods would seem much more effective in reaching individuals and
would have a greater likelihood of maximizing attendance as opposed to the posting of signs for a
one-week period at the two intersections.

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
MARCH 8, 2011
  9
 Staff is seeking direction on whether to amend the policy by implementing a “time, place, and
manner” restriction or to simply end the practice of allowing signs in the median strips.

ALTERNATIVES AVAILABLE TO THE CITY COUNCIL

  1. Review the existing policy and provide staff direction for specific revisions to implement
  time, place, and manner restrictions on the placement of signs on public property.

  2. Discontinue the City Policy and prohibit the posting of promotional and directional signs on
  public property.

RECOMMENDATION

It is recommended that the City Council review the existing policy regarding posting of promotional
and directional signs on public property and provide direction as appropriate.

CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
MARCH 8, 2011
  10

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING
  OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF

  March 8, 2011

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Palos Verdes Estates was called to order
this day at 7:30 p.m. in the City Council Chambers of City Hall by Mayor Humphrey.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

ROLL CALL:  Councilmembers Bird, Perkins, Goodhart, Mayor Pro Tem Rea,
  Mayor Humphrey

ABSENT:  None

ALSO PRESENT:  City Manager Hoefgen, City Attorney Hogin, Assistant City
  Manager Smith, Police Chief Dreiling, Public Works Director Rigg,
  Administrative Analyst Davis, Minutes Secretary Monson

MAYOR’S REPORT – Matters of Community Interest

Mayor Humphrey reminded residents that the Disaster District Program (DDP) ribbon cutting for the
final two emergency supply containers will take place on March 12th. One ceremony will be at PVHS
and the second at Montemalaga School.

CONSENT AGENDA

It was moved by Mayor Pro Tem Rea, seconded by Councilmember Perkins and unanimously
approved that the following Consent Agenda items be approved:

•  MINUTES OF THE ADJOURNED CITY COUNCIL MEETING OF FEBRUARY 15, 2011

•  MINUTES OF THE REGULAR CITY COUNCIL MEETING OF FEBRUARY 22, 2011

•  ADOPT RESOLUTION R11-07; AFFIRMING THE PLANNING COMMISSION
  APPROVAL OF NC-1400/GA-1479/M-791-10; NEIGHBORHOOD COMPATIBILITY,
  GRADING, AND MISCELLANEOUS APPLICATIONS FOR A NEW SINGLE FAMILY
  RESIDENCE LOCATED AT 700 VIA HORCADA WITH ADDITIONAL CONDITIONS.

•  APPROVE THE SPECIAL EVENT APPLICATION FOR THE AMERICAN DIABETES
  ASSOCIATION “TOUR DE CURE” TO BE HELD ON SUNDAY, MAY 1, 2011.

COMMUNICATIONS FROM THE PUBLIC - none

CITY COUNCIL  1
MARCH 8, 2011
 NEW BUSINESS

REVIEW OF CITY POLICY REGARDING POSTING OF PROMOTIONAL AND
DIRECTIONAL SIGNS ON PUBLIC PROPERTY

City Manager Hoefgen said that the report includes a significant amount of background information to
help the Council understand how the current (2006) policy came to be. The policy allows for the
placement of signs at two locations: 1) on the median strip on PVDW at Via Corta and 2) on the
median strip on PVDW across from the Lunada Bay Fountain. Currently the City receives
approximately 30 requests for posting of signs each year. There are approximately 20 signs approved
for posting annually. The current policy allows for City sponsored events and City recreational club
events. The current policy also allows for events conducted by a public entity or entities sponsored by
the Palos Verdes Peninsula School District or the Palos Verdes Library District.

City Manager Hoefgen said there is significant case law that provides guidance on the interpretation of
the first amendment’s protection of freedom of speech with regard to the City’s sign policy. The City
Attorney’s office has provided City staff guidance during this review process. Case law indicates that
the City can delineate between commercial versus non-commercial signs regarding their placement on
public property. The City can prohibit private advertising type signs. The City can also regulate the
time, place and manner of the installation of signs. The current policy identifies two locations that
signs are allowed, the size of these signs, the length of time the signs are allowed to be displayed
(currently one week) and who can install the signs (currently City staff). Staff has been receiving an
increasing number of sign requests and is having difficulty interpreting the current policy with regards
to the entities that are asking for permission to display their signs. The City has administratively placed
a hold on the installation of promotional signage while staff seeks direction from the Council. The City
is not allowed to regulate the content of the signs. Another alternative would be to end the display of
signs on public property within the City for outside or City sponsored events. The City Manager
wondered how effective these signs are in today’s electronic world.

Councilmember Goodhart said the policy was discussed in great length in 2006 and asked what
specifically is causing the problem. City Manager Hoefgen said there are additional requests that do
not fit nicely into the specified approved categories. Councilmember Goodhart asked if the worst case
scenario is that there will be a sign displayed every week of the year and if there are more than 52
requests which group has priority. City Manager Hoefgen said that is one concern – the past practice
has been that the Council would like a limited number of signs displayed which will get increasingly
more difficult with each approval as the City cannot regulate the content or number of signs.

Councilmember Bird said the current policy is on a “first come, first served” basis. He asked if staff’s
issue is that the Council will be unhappy due to the number of signs being approved and unhappiness
from the citizenry due to a sign being displayed every week. City Manager Hoefgen said that is an
issue. Councilmember Bird asked if any complaints had been received from residents regarding the
number of signs displayed by the City. City Manager Hoefgen responded that he was not aware of any
complaints. Councilmember Bird asked, again, what is causing the problem.

City Attorney Hogin interjected that the staff believes the reason the policy has specific allowable
categories was to limit the number of signs displayed in the City. As more applications are being
CITY COUNCIL  2
MARCH 8, 2011
 submitted the policy is being more and more broadly interpreted as different sub-groups of the
allowable groups are approved. The staff is asking for direction from the Council.

Mayor Humphrey said years ago there were no signs allowed within the City, then Council
implemented a sign policy sometime around 1993 and the policy has grown from that point. The
biggest concern was not to have a proliferation of signs and also to try to allow community based
organizations.

Councilmember Perkins asked if the Council could limit the number of weeks that signs are allowed to
be displayed. Attorney Hogin said that would be allowed. Councilmember Perkins said in allocating
those weeks, would it be permissible to have standing weeks for certain recurring events. Attorney
Hogin said if it is just five or six events, that would be permissible. Councilmember Perkins asked that
if such a policy was adopted and later the Council decided that, for whatever reason, the signs were
making residents unhappy, could the policy be abolished and a no-sign policy implemented. Attorney
Hogin said the Council could change the policy at any time – as long as there are other ways for groups
to get their message to residents.

Mayor Humphrey said that there could be a student group that could have a message that may be
offensive to some residents and they would be allowed to display their sign.

Mayor Pro Tem Rea said the staff recommendation is to move away from the existing policy due to
pragmatic issues in interpreting the policy and how to apply it and also due to the inadvertent impact
the current policy has on choice of speakers.

Attorney Hogin said a new policy could limit the signs to only allow City events.

Mayor Pro Tem Rea asked if this included the City concessions. Attorney Hogin said the first
amendment is a murky world – since the City owns the properties she believed this would be allowed
to a certain extent. Mayor Pro Tem Rea wondered how the City would distinguish this from
commercial speech. Attorney Hogin said commercial speech invites a commercial transaction or has a
predominately economic motivation.

Mayor Pro Tem Rea said the City cannot pick and choose which entities are allowed access.

Mayor Humphrey said this would include any organization from anywhere whether it benefits the
community or not. Attorney Hogin said any non-commercial organization.

Councilmember Bird asked if the City had received any applications in the last few years from an
organization that did not benefit the community in some way that was not from the School District or
Library and the City did not approve it. Mayor Humphrey recalled a medical marijuana group wanted
to advertise. Administrative Analyst Alexa Davis said the types of signs that are not approved are
usually from non-profit organizations promoting some type of fundraiser.

Debby Stegura from the Athletic Booster Club from Peninsula High School said she had submitted an
application to post a sign advertising the Black and Gold Affair to be held at the PV Golf Club. The
Athletic Booster Club has provided over $200,000 per year to all levels of athletics at Peninsula High
School for the past five years. The annual Black and Gold event raises about $75,000. She urged the
CITY COUNCIL  3
MARCH 8, 2011
 Council not to ban the signs altogether in PVE. She has been told by the City that the Black and Gold
Affair was not within the policy parameters. She had a letter from the School District Superintendent
that the Booster Club is a school related organization and should be considered within the sign policy.
She believes their application should have been approved.

Kathy Pape the Director of the Peninsula Education Foundation (PEF) said that utilizing the signage in
PVE is a way to make the community aware of these types of events. The PEF hopes to raise $2.5
million this year with a very small marketing budget. With the bad economy, now is not the time to
pull a valuable resource from community organizations. She understands the Council needs to a draw a
line - but asked the Council not to cut signage. She reminded the Council that the PEF supports all
kids at all Peninsula schools. She asked the Council to keep a sign policy in place.

Mayor Pro Tem Rea said Ms. Pape made a good point in that the issue is where to draw the line. He
has not had anyone complain to him about the signs so he would support modification of the policy –
time, place and manner.

Councilmember Goodhart supported limiting the number of signs and reserving specific weeks for
annual events of specific organizations. He believed the only organizations that were being denied
were organizations such as the PTA and Las Candalistas.

City Manager Hoefgen said there are various non-profits that are not school, library or City related –
such as Las Candalistas, Peninsula Chamber of Commerce, etc.

Councilmember Goodhart said it may turn into people camping out a year in advance to be sure to
reserve their desired week.

Councilmember Perkins would like to keep the signs but was not sure how to get around the first come,
first served problem and groups camping out to obtain their desired week.

Councilmember Bird was in favor of modifying the policy to reflect current legal practice. He thinks
the policy would need to continue to have a first come, first served basis or it would be too difficult on
the staff to manage. He had concerns regarding limiting the number of weeks signs would be allowed.
He supported helping community organizations that have a public purpose and benefit.

Mayor Pro Tem Rea asked if reserving certain weeks for specific organizations would be allowable.
Attorney Hogin said it is allowable if the organization is a real subset – but only six or seven or it may
seem like all weeks are pre-reserved.

Mayor Humphrey said, historically, PVE wants to support the local community and the sign policy was
put in place to make sure that the events that were promoted were local community events. The City
has been approached, in the past, by organizations that may be somewhat offensive to the community.
She wanted to make it clear that any organization anywhere could post a sign with any language they
wanted.

Councilmember Goodhart asked if the Council were to amend the policy to include only community-
based non-profit organizations – would that be permissible. Attorney Hogin said it would not as it
would be picking the speaker.
CITY COUNCIL  4
MARCH 8, 2011
 Mayor Humphrey said one of the problems staff has run into in the last year is the policy only allows
organizations that are part of the School District or Library District and there are different clubs asking
the Superintendant to be sponsored by the School District in order to skirt the policy limitations.

Councilmember Goodhart suggested the Council create a sub-committee to work with staff to modify
the policy.

Mayor Pro Tem Rea was concerned with the idea of picking and choosing organizations that are
allowed to have signs reserved for particular weeks. Councilmember Perkins shared Mayor Pro Tem
Rea’s concerns - why should one group that supports schools be allowed a reserved week over another
group that also supports schools. Councilmember Bird agreed.

Councilmember Perkins would like to open the policy up to all non-profits and reserve weeks only for
City events.

There was discussion on what is considered a City events such as National Night Out and the PVE
CARES Health Fair, but Lunada Bay and Malaga Cove Homeowners’ Association are not City events.

Mayor Humphrey said if too many outside organizations were submitting applications to post signs
then the Council could revisit the policy and decide against allowing non-profit organizations to post
signs.

Councilmember Bird asked to what extent political signage would be allowed. Attorney Hogin said
political signs would be allowed.

Councilmember Perkins asked if the City could have sign-free weeks designated. Attorney Hogin said
that would be allowed.

Councilmember Perkins asked if the City charged a fee for posting signs. Analyst Davis said there is
no fee from the City.

Mayor Pro Tem Rea suspected that the City would not need to have reserved weeks for particular
organizations as they will submit their applications way in advance.

Councilmember Goodhart asked if it made sense to have a Council sub-committee. City Manager
Hoefgen said it would be helpful to have Council’s input on a revised policy.

There was discussion about organizations that have pending applications. Council gave staff direction
to allow the Black and Gold Affair to post a sign if it they still desired to do so.

Mayor Humphrey said there was a consensus to modify the current policy to allow signage in the City
with the caveats of limiting the number of weeks in a year or assigning particular groups certain weeks,
keeping “first come, first served” and keeping the six months in advance and no later than two weeks
prior to an event timeline. The Council was not in support of charging a fee.

CITY COUNCIL  5
MARCH 8, 2011
 Mayor Humphrey said the Peninsula Education Foundation has a Fall campaign, the Black and Gold
event is usually in the Spring and those may be two groups that could have reserved weeks.

Mayor Pro Tem Rea asked if Council was giving direction to staff to give priority to certain groups.
Councilmember Goodhart believed it was not allowed. Mayor Humphrey believed certain weeks
could be assigned to specific groups. Attorney Hogin said that the Council could have a policy that is
“first come, first served” but certain designated weeks be set aside for some annual events.

Mayor Humphrey asked City Manager Hoefgen if he would prefer to put together a draft policy with
the City Attorney or would he prefer a Council sub-committee also. City Manager Hoefgen said he
would prefer to work with a sub-committee.

There was discussion regarding revisiting the policy if the tone and tenor of the signs became
overwhelmingly negative or controversial.

City Manager asked the Council for volunteers to serve on the sub-committee. Mayor Humphrey and
Mayor Pro Tem Rea will serve on the Council ad-hoc committee to review the sign policy.

It was moved by Councilmember Goodhart, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Rea and unanimously
approved to continue the review of the existing policy regarding posting of promotional and directional
signs on public property and to have Mayor Humphrey and Mayor Pro Tem Rea serve as the ad-hoc
committee to assist staff in drafting a revised sign policy for future consideration by the Council.
